html:
Roman lawyer, statesman and writer, the greatest orator of the Republic. Like Marius he came from Arpinum and was a "new man" with no consuls in his family.

He made his name in 70 BCE by prosecuting Verres, a corrupt governor of Sicily. As consul in 63 BCE he exposed Catiline's conspiracy and had five plotters executed without trial, which got him exiled for a year in 58 BCE.

He hated rule by strong men but had to live with them. He would not join the First Triumvirate, sided with Pompey in the civil war, and was pardoned by Caesar. After Caesar's murder he attacked Mark Antony in fourteen speeches called the Philippics. When the Second Triumvirate was formed in 43 BCE, Antony had him put on the death lists. He was killed at Formiae, and his head and hands were nailed up in the Forum.

His speeches, essays and some nine hundred letters made Latin prose what it became. Works like On the Republic carried Greek philosophy into Latin. When Petrarch found his letters to Atticus in 1345, Cicero became a model for the humanists of the Renaissance.
sum: Roman lawyer, statesman and writer, the greatest orator of the Republic. Like Marius he came from Arpinum and was a "new man" with no consuls in his family.
